title_en: Stories of Modern China (17/20): The Year of the Flood
note_en: 着 after a verb can describe a lasting state, especially in sentences that say what exists somewhere: 镇口立着一块石碑 "at the entrance to the town stands a stone tablet," and 上面刻着……名字 "carved on it are the names." Here the place comes first and the thing comes last, much like English "There's a tablet standing at the entrance," and 着 tells you the result of the action is still there.
